actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: seed

facts.text: The default robot is panda_wristcam, the initial joint-position noise is 0.02, and the task holds 5 cans
The supported robots are panda_wristcam, panda and fetch
The can model is scaled by 0.03 with radius 1 m and height 3.5 m
The can xy positions start from torch.rand((b, 2)) * 0.26 - 0.13 and are sampled in the region [-0.15, -0.15] to [0.15, 0.15]
Equal spacing passes when at least one of the two smallest pairwise distance gaps is at most 0.01
The linear arrangement is tested only for 3 cans, with an area tolerance of 0.001
Success requires equal spacing, a linear arrangement and no grasped can
The dense reaching reward is 2 * (1 - tanh(5 * min_dist)) from the TCP to the nearest can
When obs_mode contains state the observation adds the TCP pose, each can pose, the TCP-to-can and the can-to-can position vectors
The base camera is 512x512 with a pi/2 field of view, near plane 0.01 and far plane 100
The robot base is placed at [-0.615, 0, 0]

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's initial can positions; the fake is deterministic for one seed, but it draws with Python's random.Random while ManiSkill draws with torch's RNG, so a seed gives different coordinates on the two

gaps: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuator or sensor model: the fake only tracks can xy positions and the task score; the SAPIEN scene, the Panda arm and gripper, collisions and the mplib planner are not modelled

the action space and observation arrays are inherited from ManiSkill's BaseEnv and the Panda agent, which are external to the clone; the fake exposes neither space, so the step action is accepted as an open object with no shape or bounds (NOT COVERED: the full action and observation arrays and the camera images)
the can placement uses uniform sampling with rejection in the declared region; upstream uses ManiSkill's UniformPlacementSampler and torch's RNG, so one seed gives different coordinates
timestep_ms is 0 because the clone does not state ManiSkill's control timestep; ticks count fake transitions, not simulated seconds
no rendering and no snapshots; the fake was never compared with the upstream environment because ManiSkill and SAPIEN were not installed where the gate ran

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
